builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Leto: Utility-Centric Agent Memory
summary: Leto replaces fidelity-based agent memory (store faithful summaries, retrieve by similarity) with utility-centric memory: index conversation sources, replay anticipated context per request, and refine selection using response outcomes. It costs an indexing and replay pipeline plus an outcome-feedback utility loop, adding system complexity and per-request retrieval overhead, though it can reduce served context tokens relative to raw-history retrieval. It can fail when future requests diverge from what the replay anticipates, when the outcome signal is noisy or unavailable, or on workloads without recurring user context where simpler retrieval suffices.
rationale: Utility-driven memory selection improves personalization and long-horizon task quality and runs via APIs and lightweight indexing, but its gains must be validated on the reader's own agent workloads before production reliance.
technique: Utility-centric agent memory with replay loop

claims.statement: Leto replaces fidelity-based agent memory (store faithful summaries, retrieve by similarity) with utility-centric memory: index conversation sources, replay anticipated context per request, and refine selection using response outcomes. It costs an indexing and replay pipeline plus an outcome-feedback utility loop, adding system complexity and per-request retrieval overhead, though it can reduce served context tokens relative to raw-history retrieval. It can fail when future requests diverge from what the replay anticipates, when the outcome signal is noisy or unavailable, or on workloads without recurring user context where simpler retrieval suffices.

Outperforms the strongest baseline by 16.3 percentage points accuracy on PrefEval and 3.1 points task completion on PERMA; best overall on MemoryArena; on par with raw-history retrieval for long-context understanding while serving fewer context tokens.
